cover.today: Nvidia’s top chips turn up in Shanghai, India plans 3,300 GPUs in Pune, and why inference is the real bill.
cover.headline: Too big to smuggle. Found anyway.
cover.dek: Bloomberg found Nvidia’s top Blackwell rack, which needs a US licence for China, in Shanghai filings. Plus 2 more things that moved in AI.

scoreAka: aka. 3 stories, and how true each one is

summary.text: Nvidia’s top Blackwell rack shows up in Shanghai filings.
MeitY: ~3,300 GPUs for Pune, an inference subsidy next.
Training vs inference: where the AI bill really lives.

summaryNote: US on holiday. No big funding round.

slides.wit: Too big to smuggle. Found anyway.
slides.plain: Bloomberg found Nvidia’s top rack, a GB300 NVL72, in Chinese loan filings for a Shanghai data centre. How it got there isn’t known.
slides.sowhat: One rack was pledged as collateral for a 96 million yuan (~$14M) loan. AI chips are now treated like gold bars.
slides.src: Bloomberg, 27 Nov 2026, via The Next Web, Anadolu, Benzinga · Nvidia’s CEO said in May 2025 these systems were too big to smuggle

il.left: EACH DOT = 100 GPUs · C-DAC PUNE, ABOUT 3,300

slides.plain: MeitY Secretary S. Krishnan says C-DAC Pune is setting up about 3,300 GPUs and Bengaluru gets a 30-petaflop machine. Next: a scheme to subsidise inference.
slides.sowhat: IndiaAI support is for training today. Cheaper inference would mean Indian startups pay less each time a user hits ‘send’.
slides.realNote: plan announced · scheme not out yet
slides.src: Remarks at Tec-Verse 2026, reported by NewsBytes and others · 27 Nov · no official MeitY document yet

slides.aka: aka. why the india story matters
slides.wit: Training is school. Inference is the job.
slides.plain: Training teaches a model once, at huge cost. Inference is every answer it gives after that, and that meter never stops.
slides.aside: School fees once. Electricity bill forever.
slides.sowhat: That’s why MeitY now talks about inference: a popular Indian app runs its model all day, so that’s where the money goes.
slides.src: Explainer · ties to today’s MeitY remarks

slides.plain: Both of today’s stories are about the same thing: who is allowed to have AI chips, and who builds their own.
slides.p: The race isn’t only better models. It’s who controls the chips, and who pays every time a model answers.

slides.k: My take · as an AI PM
slides.t: the demo is cheap. the meter isn’t.
slides.sub: why inference cost decides which indian AI products survive
p: when i build an ai feature, nobody in the demo asks about cost. three months later, finance asks about the monthly inference bill. every chat and every summary keeps the meter running.
that’s why today’s meity remark matters more than it sounds. if the government helps with inference, indian startups can price for indian wallets.
my advice to founders: track cost per answer like you track latency. if one use costs more than a user pays you in a day, the feature won’t survive at scale.
